panels.rationale: Patient-derived H&E histopathology from the mandibular lesion shows dense sheets of plasma cells, supported directly by the caption and article text as the diagnostic basis for solitary plasmacytoma. Green circles and a scale bar are present as figure annotations.

in_text_mentions: Under local anesthetic and sterile settings, an intraosseous incisional specimen, consisting of the premolar tooth and various pieces of soft and hard cream-brown tissue measuring 1*1*0.4 cm in total, was obtained through a complete mucoperiosteal flap. Multiple plasma cell sheets were observed in the primary sample (Figure 2). Immunohistochemistry staining for CD138 showed a positive reaction in plasmacytoid cells, which confirmed the plasmacytoma diagnosis. The second procedure was an excision, followed by a bone marrow aspiration and a biopsy to rule out multiple myeloma.

The liver biopsy exhibited abnormal plasma cells in periportal locations with lambda light chain restriction as well; Congo red stain was not done on the liver sample.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel A shows H&E staining of bone marrow with sheets of plasma cells, a classic histologic feature of plasmacytoma. B: Panel B shows H&E staining of the skull base mass with dense plasma cell infiltration, characteristic of extramedullary plasmacytoma. C: Panel C shows immunohistochemical positivity for lambda light chain, demonstrating light-chain restriction in the plasmacytoma. D: Panel D shows immunohistochemical negativity for kappa light chain, confirming lambda light-chain restriction in the plasmacytoma.

in_text_mentions: Given the progression of visual field defects, a decision was made to arrange emergent transsphenoidal biopsy, which revealed sheets of plasma cells with lambda light-chain restriction consistent with plasmacytoma. Bone marrow biopsy was performed again to diagnose multiple myeloma, which revealed sheets of plasma cells with lambda restriction without staining for kappa light chain on immunohistochemistry. Patchy moderate to a marked increase in reticulin fibers were seen on reticulin stain with an increase in stainable iron on the iron stain (Figures 4A-4D).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (a, b, c, d, e, f). a: Low-power H&E stain showing tumor invasion of periureteral soft tissue, consistent with extramedullary plasmacytoma infiltration pattern. [raw subtype: extramedullary] b: High-power H&E stain demonstrating plasmacytoma-like atypical cells with high nuclear-cytoplasmic ratio, characteristic of plasma cell neoplasms. [raw subtype: extramedullary] c: Immunohistochemistry demonstrating CD138 positivity in tumor cells, confirming plasma cell lineage. [raw subtype: extramedullary] d: Immunohistochemistry showing CD79a/mb-1 positivity in tumor cells, supporting B-cell lineage differentiation. [raw subtype: extramedullary] e: Immunohistochemistry demonstrating weak Igκ light chain expression in tumor cells. [raw subtype: extramedullary] f: Immunohistochemistry demonstrating strong Igλ light chain expression with light chain restriction (Igλ > Igκ), confirming clonal plasma cell proliferation. [raw subtype: extramedullary]

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: H&E staining demonstrating the characteristic morphological feature of extramedullary plasmacytoma: sheet-like infiltration by atypical monomorphic plasma cells in the nasopharyngeal subepithelial tissue. B: CD138 immunohistochemistry demonstrating diffuse positivity, confirming plasma cell lineage and supporting the diagnosis of extramedullary plasmacytoma. C: Kappa light chain immunostaining showing light chain restriction, demonstrating clonality of the plasma cell proliferation in extramedullary plasmacytoma. D: Pan-CK (AE1/AE3) immunostaining showing negativity in tumor cells (while neighboring epithelium is positive), excluding carcinoma and confirming the non-epithelial nature of the plasmacytoma. E: CD20 immunostaining showing negativity in tumor cells, excluding B-cell lymphoma and supporting the plasma cell neoplasm diagnosis. F: EBER in situ hybridization showing negativity in tumor cells, excluding EBV-associated...

panels.figure_caption: Histological and immunohistological features of the second nasopharyngeal biopsy. a. Subepithelial tissue was infiltrated by sheets of a monotonous population consisting of medium-sized atypical plasmacytoid cells without syncytial cell islands. b. immunohistochemical staining showed that the plasmacytoid cells were diffusely positive to CD138 and kappa light chain c, but they were negative to pan-CK (AE1/AE3) (the neighboring epithelium was positive to pan-CK) d, CD20 e and not reactive to EBERs detection f. a, HE staining with original magnification × 400; b-e, immunohistochemical staining with original magnification × 400; f, in situ hybridization for EBERs with original magnification × 400)
in_text_mentions: But they were negative to CD20, CD21, CD3, and CD5. EBV detection by in situ hybridization for EBERs showed the nuclear positive only in syncytial cell islands, and the plasmacytoid cells were EBV-negative. In the second nasopharyngeal biopsy, subepithelial tissue was infiltrated by sheets of a monotonous population consisting of medium-sized atypical plasmacytoid cells without syncytial cell islands. Immunohistochemically, the tumor cells were strongly positive for CD79a, CD138, CD38 and MUM-1, as well as the presence of kappa light chain restriction. EBV detection was non-reactive (Fig. 3).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A is an orthopantomograph (radiograph) of a human patient with solitary plasmacytoma, showing bilateral ill-defined radiolucent lesions in the mandible consistent with expansile osteolytic bone lesions of the disease, with associated root resorption of involved teeth as noted in the article text. B: Panel B is a cone-beam CT scan of the same patient with solitary plasmacytoma, demonstrating bilateral expansile lytic lesions with irregular borders involving the mandible, consistent with the radiological manifestations of the disease.

panels.figure_caption: A – Orthopantomograph showing ill-defined radiolucency with respect to tooth numbers 31 to 38 and 45 to 48; B – CBCT showing the presence of bilateral expansile lytic lesions with irregular borders.
in_text_mentions: An orthopantomograph revealed the presence of bilateral ill-defined radiolucent lesions. The left-side lesion showed the involvement of the entire mandible extending from tooth number 31 to the ramus. Root resorption of involved teeth was noted. The right side showed a radiolucent lesion around the periapical area of 46 and the interdental area of 45 and 46 (Figure 2A). Cone-beam Computed Tomography (CBCT) revealed expansile lytic lesions with irregular borders. The periapical area in relation to 41 and 42 was spared (Figure 2B).

panels.rationale: Histopathology image (H&E, ×400) showing sheet of neoplastic plasma cells with eccentric nuclei and dense eosinophilic cytoplasm, consistent with solitary plasmacytoma. The case is specifically described as anaplastic solitary plasmacytoma of the mandible. [raw subtype: anaplastic]

in_text_mentions: CBCT) revealed a large destructive lesion of the left mandible involving the body of the mandible and condylar processes (Fig. 1A and 1B). The skull and pelvis radiographic survey failed to identify additional osseous lesions. Complete blood count and coagulation tests were within normal limits. His past medical history was unremarkable. An incisional biopsy was performed under local anesthesia. Histopathologic examination of the specimen revealed proliferation of plasmacytoid cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm, hyperchromatic nuclei, cellular pleomorphism with mitotic figures (Fig.2).
